This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 13.09.2017 at about 6.15 p.m, when the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider with her husband Sri.Narayanaswamy were on the way to their residence from Kithaganur to Haraluru village in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-R-4117 and proceeding slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When they reached near Gajendra Hallow brick factory, Bettakote villate on Devanahalli - Budigere Main road,
C.R.Patna Hobli, Bengaluru at that time driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MG-5143 which was driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life came from opposite side i.e., from Devanahalli side and dashed the petitioner's motorcycle.

As a result of which she sustained grievous injuries and after the accident she was shifted to near by Hospital wherein she took first aid treatement, then she was shifted to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru wherein she took treatment as inpatient and underwent surgery and she was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
She has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that, at the time of accident she was working at Adityavani Facility Services and earning Rs.8,525/- p.m.
It is specifically urged that, due to the said accident she lost her earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.

The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and driver and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a Narasamma vs Chandrakala on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91032813/
2 compensation amount.

sentences.text: 3. After registering the case, notices were issued to the respondents.
Respondents No.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel and filed common objections denying the petition averments.
They specifically contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondents denied that at the time of accident they are owner and driver of the car.

Per contra contended that the rider of the two wheeler who was not competent to drive the said vehicle has driven the same in a rash and negligent manner caused the accident by hitting a road side pole and due to which petitioner sustained injuries.

Further respondents contended that the car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MG-5143 was not at all involved in the accident, as the same was not in a usable condition since March-2017 and it was sold as scrap to a scarp dealer and scrap dealer took the same and put the same at his garage near Devanahalli.

The petitioner somehow got the number plate of the car near the garage, colluding with the police have falsely implicated the case in order to get wrongful gain from this respondents, knowing that the vehicle was not having valid insurance policy the petitioner is prosecuting against the owner of the car in present case.
It is contended that the car number plate was stated as recovered by the police during spot mahazar.
Hence the IMV was not done to the respondent vehicle.

Further the respondents stated that in IMV Report it is clearly mentioned the damages caused to the motorcycle, in the IMV report the RTO has requested to verify the validity of records of the vehicles and the same was not done property and charge sheet was not prepared on the said facts by the investigation officer.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that she sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 13.09.2017 at about 6.15 p.m., near Bettakote village, on Budigere- Devanahalli road, C.R.Patna Hobli, Bengaluru District due to actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA- 03-MG-5143 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
5. The husband/next friend of the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .P1 to 22 were marked on behalf of the petitioner.

Dr.Sunil V Furtado, Professor & HOD of Neurosurgery at M.S.
Ramaiah Hospital
was examined as PW.2.
Ex.P23 to 28 were marked through him.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.1/owner of the car herself examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 & 2 documents.

3
6. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.1 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

7. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1: The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by husband of petitioner, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed chargesheet against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-03- MG-5143 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338,
201 of IPC & u/s 196, 187 of IMV Act.
9.
It is not in dispute that the car is owned by the respondent No.1.
It is urged by the respondent No.1 that, the said car is not at all involved in the accident.
According to the version of respondent No.1, that the offending car is falsely implicated in this case so as to wangle the compensation amount.
The whole defence of the respondent No.1 is that the car was not at all involved in the accident and the husband of the petitioner was riding the two wheeler and caused the accident.
In order to disprove the contention, the respondent No.1 herself examined as RW.1.
She reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
During the course of her cross examination she categorically admitted that she is the owner of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MG-5143 for 1 to 1 months.
The RC was also standing in her name but she denied that who was driving the car on the date of accident.
Further she has not produced any documents with regard to the offending vehicle.

Further she stated that 4 to 5 years back the Channarayapatna police has intimated her about the occurrence of accident and thereafter she enquired with police but the police have hoodwinked her and took her signatures on various papers.
She deposed that she could not recollect when she had purchased the car.

Further she stated that she sold the car for Rs.30,000/- by way of cash but she did not have any documents to show that she have sold the car and she had not given intimation to the RTO and she has also not maintained any documents for selling the car.
She has signed one form after selling her car and she did not know the identity of the purchaser.
RW.1 stated that the assurance given by the police is the base of her say in para No.4 of her affidavit with regard to the implanting of number plate by securing it from the garage.

Further she stated that she did not know whether the purchaser had purchase the car for scrap or to use on his own and she did not know the garage address, person who purchased the car and such other details.
The garage people are responsible fore the accident and she did not taken any legal action against the garage people.
On conspectus reading of the above said version of the RW.1 one thing is clear that she is the owner of the car as on the date of accident.
The petition averments discloses that due to the negligent driving of the car petitioner sustained injuries.
Furthermore the medical records discloses that the accident happened because of negligent driving of the car by its driver.

When such being the case, the accident happened while she was proceeding as a pillion rider it can be easily in the absence of other material placed on record can be concluded that there is a involvement of the offending car in the accident.

Another important aspect which needs consideration is Ex.P.2 being the complaint which Narasamma vs Chandrakala on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91032813/
4 is also filed next day of accident.
The MLC discloses that on the date of accident itself the said MLC was entered.
The said document also came from proper custody.
Having regard to the attending circumstances and such other circumstances surround in the case it can be easily conclude that the involvement of the car in the accident.
10. The next seminal question to be considered whether delay of one day in setting criminal law into motion is fatal to the case of the petitioner.
It is relevant to note that, as per the version of the petitioner the accident happened on 13.09.2017 at about 6.15 p.m.
As per the contents of Ex.P.2 the criminal law was set into the motion on 14.09.2017 at 11.00 a.m.
The PW.2 has produced the case sheet / MLC.
On close perusal of the MLC extract it reflects about the manner of the accident and time of the accident.
In the presence of this document the delay of one day is not at all fatal to the case of the petitioner.
The medical records discloses that the petitioner was badly injured in the accident.
In view of contents in Ex.P.5 wound certificate the delay of 1 day is self explanatory.
There is a delay of 1 day and that delay is well explained by the petitioner.

In this regard it is relevant to rely on the decision reported in Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226,
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed as hereunder :

entities.text: Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "The purpose of lodging the FIR in motor accident cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquillity of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if there is delay, the same deserve to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."
(Emphasis supplied by me).
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The ratio decidendi laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court is aptly applicable to the facts of the instant case.
The petitioner had explained the delay caused.

Narasamma vs Chandrakala on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91032813/
5 11.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even here in this case the driver of the car is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of car and he was charge sheeted.
On the evidence of PW.1 and Ex.P.6 charge sheet clearly reveals that the accident occurred due to rash and negligence of driver of car.
Though PW.1 was cross-examined at length by respondent No.1 counsel but nothing fatal was elicited so as to distrust the petitioner's version in his chief-examination.
The petitioner has satisfactorily proved that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of the car in the accident.

Therefore, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 'In the Affirmative'.
12. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the car.
Therefore she is entitled for compensation.
13. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME : In the Aadhaar card (Ex.P19) the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 24.03.1972.
This indicates that she was aged 45 years on the date of accident.

PW.1 has deposed that prior to the accident his wife was working as an employee of Adityavani Facility Services Pvt Ltd., HRBR Layout, Kalyanana Nagar, Bengaluru and thereby drawing a gross salary of Rs.8,525/- p.m.
In order to prove the said fact, the PW.1 has produced the computer generated salary slip at Ex.P.8 for the month of July-2017.
But in order to substantiate the said fact the author of the document is not examined.
However if considered the notional income as per the notional income table issued by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and Karnataka State Legal Service Authority it comes to Rs.11,000/-.
But in the present case, the petitioner herself admitted that her income is Rs.8,525/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.

14. As per the medical records petitioner has sustained the following injuries :
i. severe head injury H/o loss of consciousness and right ear bleed.
A lecerated wound on right parietal region 3x2 cm present.
CT Scam brain showed (a) diffuse cerebral oedema (b) fracture of right petrous temporal bone (c) left tempero parietal SDH and contusion, cisters obliterated.
ii. A cut lacerated wound on right ankle 2x 1 cm.

Narasamma vs Chandrakala on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91032813/
6 15.
It is needless to say that the injury No.1 is grievous in nature.
As per the medical records the petitioner was initially taken to near by hospital and thereafter she was shifted to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru, where she was admitted as an inpatient.

The discharge summary as per Ex.P.23 and Ex.P.7, the petitioner was admitted in the said hospital from 13.09.2017 to 23.09.2017,
06.12.2017 to 07.12.2017, 12.12.2017 to 15.12.2017 for the period of (11+2+4=17 days in total).
During the course of treatment she underwent surgeries in the form of : 1) Left FTP decompressive craniectomy and evacuation of SDH with evacuation of temporal contusion done under GA on 14.09.2014.
2) Crampoplasty autologous on 13.12.2017, post operatively she recovered well, with no deficits and is being discharged with following advice.
At the time of discharge her condition is stable.
16. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES: The period of hospitalization of 17 days is proved with the help of Discharge summary.

During her stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied her to the hospital to take her care by leaving their duties.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.750/- per day and a sum of Rs.12,750/- (750 X 17) is awarded under this head.
17. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
The petitioner has sustained severe traumatic brain injury.
As such she would have had undergone pain and mental agony.

Hence the petitioner is entitled to Rs.1,00,000/-
under this head.

18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, her line and duration of treatment, it is quite natural that petitioner was forced to remain absent from her work for a period of 10 months atleast.
Thus by taking into account the income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.85,250/- (Rs.8,525 X 10) under this head.
19. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
It is the specific assertion of PW.1 that owing to the accidental injuries the petitioner has become permanently disabled and has thereby lost her earning capacity.
Therefore Dr. Sunil V Furtado, Professor and HOD of Neurosurgery at M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru was examined as PW.2.
This witness stated that on 06.02.2023 he examined the petitioner for disability assessment.

On examination he found that Glascow coma stage : 15/15, Pupils : Bilateral equal and reactive to light, mild speech disability - 25% cranial nerves normal - vision and lower cranial nerves normal, No limb weakness, motor system / sensory system - Normal.
The CT Scan of the brain of petitioner was done on 06.02.2023 and it showed Gliosis in the left temporal and high frontal lobe with post operative surgeries.
Her neuropsychological assessment done on 09.02.2023 showed mini mental status examination 20/30, montreal cognitive assessment 15/30.
Behavioural personality : mild level difficulty.
ADL : Independent.

Left frontal Narasamma vs Chandrakala on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91032813/
7 lobe and bilateral temporal lobe involvement.
More involvement of left fronto temporal lobe moderate level cognitive disability.
Disability rate - 50%.
Very severe level disability.
According to the DGHS guidelines and based on his examination, PW.2 has opined that the petitioner has a permanent neurological disability of 62.5%.

20. Be that as it may, all injuries and assessment of disability do not impact the earning capacity,
nor in a similar way.
The disability has to be seen in the context of the particular occupation or calling that the victim is engaged in.

The co-relation between the physical disability suffered in an accident and the loss of earning capacity resulting from it was considered in great detail by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar V/s Ajaykumar and another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

entities.text: Rajkumar V/s Ajaykumar and another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the Apex Court held that it is the functional disability which would be the operative criteria for assessing the loss of future earnings and not the physical disability.

21. In the instant case if the say of PW.2 that prior to the accident the petitioner was working as a house keeper is believed to be true then neurological disability at 62.5% vitally affects not only her working capacity but also her livelihood.
To put it differently, the earning capacity of the petitioner as on the date of the accident stands completely negated and not reduced.
Therefore compensation for loss of future earning has to be just and proper so as to enable her to live a life of dignity.
On appreciation of the evidence on record, the loss of earning capacity of the petitioner according to this Tribunal may be as high as 100%, but in no case it would be less than 40%.
Accordingly the compensation for the loss of the petitioner's future earning must be computed on that basis.
The appropriate multiplier applicable as per Sarla verma's case is '14'.
Thus Future loss of income is awarded at Rs.5,72,880/- (Rs.8,525 X 12 X 14 X 40/100) which is rounded off to Rs.5,73,000/-.

22. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of her life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face disappointment and frustration & also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures and joys of human life.
The petitioner would now become dependent on her family members for her entire life.
Considering all these factors a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded under this head.
23. MEDICAL EXPENSES :
PW.1 has produced 42- medical bills at Ex.P9.
As per that, he has spent Rs.3,75,420/- towards medical expenses of the petitioner.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the cross-examination of PW.1, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled to Rs.3,75,420/- which is rounded off to Rs.3,75,500/- towards medical expenses.
24. LOSS OF FUTURE PROSPECTS:
The condition of the petitioner would affect her future prospects both professionally and personally.
For the loss that the petitioner shall suffer in this regard ends of justice would be met if he is awarded a compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- under this head.

8
25. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.

26. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra : 12,750-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain and sufferings : 1,00,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 85,250-00 period 4 Loss of future income due to : 5,73,000-00 disability 5 Loss of future amenities & :
1,00,000-00 happiness 6

Medical Expenses : 3,75,500-00 7 Loss of future prospects :
2,00,000-00 8
Future medical expenses : - Nil - Total 14,46,500-00 27.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
28. The respondent No.1 is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle.
She has not produced any document to show that her vehicle had insurance coverage at the time of accident.
It is well settled that a person driving a vehicle is presumed to have authority to do the same unless the contrary is proved.

In the absence of any contrary evidence in this regard and also considering the fact that the claimant has established that the accident was caused by the driver of the offending vehicle (respondent No.2 herein), the respondent No.1 is vicariously liable to pay the compensation awarded by this Tribunal.
Hence she is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

Therefore this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
29. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,46,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to her through NEFT/ RTGS by Narasamma vs Chandrakala on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91032813/
9 way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.

opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that she sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 13.09.2017 at about 6.15 p.m., near Bettakote village, on Budigere- Devanahalli road, C.R.Patna Hobli, Bengaluru District due to actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA- 03-MG-5143 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
10. The next seminal question to be considered whether delay of one day in setting criminal law into motion is fatal to the case of the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The petition averments discloses that due to the negligent driving of the car petitioner sustained injuries.
Furthermore the medical records discloses that the accident happened because of negligent driving of the car by its driver.
When such being the case, the accident happened while she was proceeding as a pillion rider it can be easily in the absence of other material placed on record can be concluded that there is a involvement of the offending car in the accident.
Having regard to the attending circumstances and such other circumstances surround in the case it can be easily conclude that the involvement of the car in the accident.
In the presence of this document the delay of one day is not at all fatal to the case of the petitioner.
The medical records discloses that the petitioner was badly injured in the accident.
In view of contents in Ex.P.5 wound certificate the delay of 1 day is self explanatory.
There is a delay of 1 day and that delay is well explained by the petitioner.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.
If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The ratio decidendi laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court is aptly applicable to the facts of the instant case.
The petitioner had explained the delay caused.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
The disability has to be seen in the context of the particular occupation or calling that the victim is engaged in.
21. In the instant case if the say of PW.2 that prior to the accident the petitioner was working as a house keeper is believed to be true then neurological disability at 62.5% vitally affects not only her working capacity but also her livelihood.
To put it differently, the earning capacity of the petitioner as on the date of the accident stands completely negated and not reduced.
Therefore compensation for loss of future earning has to be just and proper so as to enable her to live a life of dignity.
Accordingly the compensation for the loss of the petitioner's future earning must be computed on that basis.
The appropriate multiplier applicable as per Sarla verma's case is '14'.
28. The respondent No.1 is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle.
She has not produced any document to show that her vehicle had insurance coverage at the time of accident.
It is well settled that a person driving a vehicle is presumed to have authority to do the same unless the contrary is proved.
In the absence of any contrary evidence in this regard and also considering the fact that the claimant has established that the accident was caused by the driver of the offending vehicle (respondent No.2 herein), the respondent No.1 is vicariously liable to pay the compensation awarded by this Tribunal.
opennyai_summary.arguments: It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
